subject: Clarify training guarantees, retention windows, and deletion process
messages:
From: Alex Anderson <alex.anderson@acme-payments.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Qs on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has two short items they need clarified before we move to procurement: 1) Acme needs an explicit, written assurance that Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train or improve its hosted models (we understand private deployments are different) and 2) a clear table of retention windows (request logs, request bodies, KV caches, backups, and backups retention/deletion process).

Can you provide: a one-paragraph plain-language assurance we can share with our legal team, plus an itemized retention table? Also, can you confirm whether deletion requests via the API remove all copies (including short-term backups) and roughly how long that purge takes?

Appreciate fast turnaround — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Anderson
Security Engineer, Acme Payments
security@acme-payments.com

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Anderson <alex.anderson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Rishi and Laura are looped for contract and infra specifics. I attached a short summary PDF and a retention table spreadsheet.

Plain-language assurance (shareable):
Redwood does not use customer-provided content from your API requests or S3 uploads to train or improve our public/shared foundation models. Customer content may be processed for inference and short-lived operational uses (e.g., caching to serve a session), but we do not incorporate identifiable customer data into model training datasets for hosted customers. Aggregated, anonymized telemetry (usage metrics, error rates, model selection statistics) may be used to improve service reliability and product features. For customers who require additional guarantees, Redwood offers Private deployments and contractual DPA clauses that restrict product-improvement telemetry.

Retention highlights (see attached spreadsheet for full rows):
- Request bodies: default retention 30 days; can be shortened via customer config or DPA.
- Request metadata / logs: retained 180 days for audit and billing; aggregated metrics retained longer (up to 24 months).
- KV cache / session prefixes: cached for active session durations; evicted per TTL policies (default: 24 hours) unless customer pins cache in Private deployments.
- Backups and snapshots: standard backups retained up to 90 days; deletion requests initiate removal processes that clear live copies within 24 hours and purges backups per backup retention window (typically completed within 90 days).

Deletion process: when a customer submits a deletion request (API or Console), we mark customer content for deletion immediately and purge live stores within 24 hours. Backups are scheduled for removal per backup retention windows; we provide an attestation and a timeline for completion. For stricter guarantees, customers can select shorter backup retention in Dedicated/Private plans and require contractual commitments.

Laura — can you add any infra notes about KMS/backups and actual purge mechanics? Rishi — can you propose DPA language for the one-paragraph assurance and a clause that covers backup purge timing?

Next step: if Acme wants a redlineable clause we can send today, or schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the attachments.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_NoTrain_Summary.pdf, data-retention-table.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Anderson <alex.anderson@acme-payments.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Alex / Monica — quick infra clarifications from the ops side:

- KMS/backups: Customer keys for Private deployments can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-KMS). For Hosted customers, service-managed KMS is used; access to key material is controlled and logged. Backups that contain encrypted customer data are encrypted at rest; Redwood personnel do not have access to plaintext without customer authorization and established procedures.

- Purge mechanics: Deletion requests trigger a coordinated job that deletes from primary storage (S3) and clears caches within 24 hours. Backup snapshots are indexed; an internal retention manager schedules eligible snapshots for deletion during the next maintenance window. In practice, most backup artifacts referencing deleted objects become unrecoverable within 30–90 days depending on the snapshot lifecycle.

- Evidence: we can provide an internal runbook excerpt and backup lifecycle diagram under NDA or as redacted artifacts.

Laura Bennett
Head of Infrastructure Operations
laura@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Anderson <alex.anderson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on 'we do not train on customer data' and retention windows

Alex — adding legal language you can drop into a contract or DPA:

"Redwood represents and warrants that it will not use Customer Content submitted to the Redwood hosted inference service to train, improve, or otherwise develop Redwood's shared or public models. For the avoidance of doubt, Customer Content will not be incorporated into datasets used for model training. Redwood may collect and retain aggregated and anonymized telemetry for product and service improvement. Customer may request deletion of Customer Content, and Redwood will delete live copies within 24 hours of a valid deletion request and will schedule deletion of backups in accordance with Redwood's backup retention policy (standard maximum 90 days), with an attestation provided upon completion."

If you want, I attached a suggested DPA clause (DPA_clause_suggestion.docx) and can push this through DocuSign once you confirm. Note that enterprise customers can negotiate shorter backup windows or explicit no-backup clauses for higher compliance tiers (typically in Dedicated/Private plans).

Rishi Malhotra
